quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Your body removes alcohol at what rate?

options.text: About one drink per hour.
About two drinks per hour.
About three drinks per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: On average, your body removes alcohol from about one drink per hour. This rate varies from person to person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Is texting and driving allowed?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
Yes, when stopped at a red light.
Yes, when there is little traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is very dangerous and increases crash risk by up to 23 times. South Dakota law makes texting while driving illegal.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride at the same speed as during the day.
Ride slower than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on unfamiliar roads. Riding slower gives you more time to spot and avoid hazards when you cannot see as well.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycle and car conflicts happen most often.

questions.question: Which item does NOT help protect you in a crash?

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet.
A leather jacket.
A sweatshirt.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather jacket or sturdy synthetic jacket also offers protection. A sweatshirt does not provide crash protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If there are hazards to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?

options.text: Right side
Left side
Either side

questions.correctAnswerText: Left side
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space away from hazards. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything you need to see.
Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot.
Signal and immediately move to the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and turn your head to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always use your mirrors AND turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle mirrors?

options.text: They show you everything around your motorcycle.
They do not show your blind spots.
You should only use them when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding near a truck, what does it mean if you cannot see the truck's mirrors?

options.text: The truck driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on riding and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid staying in the blind spots of large trucks. If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you either.

questions.question: When someone is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to return to your lane too quickly, which is also dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help other drivers see you.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning makes you more visible and helps you avoid hazards. It also discourages other drivers from entering your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Your face only, not your eyes.
Your eyes only, not your whole face.
Your entire face, including your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire face, including your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes during a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles traveling under 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction machinery, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: Is it safe to take over-the-counter medication before riding?

options.text: Yes, over-the-counter drugs are always weak.
Yes, it is always acceptable.
Maybe not. These medications can affect your riding ability and require caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maybe not. These medications can affect your riding ability and require caution.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter and prescription medications have side effects that can impair your riding ability. Always ask your doctor how a new medication might affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: If a driver makes eye contact with you, does that mean they have seen you?

options.text: Yes, you know they have seen you.
Not necessarily. They may not have actually noticed you.
Yes, and they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not necessarily. They may not have actually noticed you.
questions.explanation: Eye contact does not guarantee a driver has seen you. Many drivers look directly at motorcyclists without actually noticing them. Never depend on eye contact to keep you safe.

questions.question: When someone is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is generally safest when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the rear brake before the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes together when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on dry pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle as long as it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the edge of the road mean?

options.text: No parking allowed.
The right edge of the traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the edge of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving as separate actions, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can make your motorcycle fall over.

questions.question: When scanning the area around your motorcycle, what should you look for?

options.text: Escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
Whether you can drive faster than other vehicles.
Pedestrians to stare at.

questions.correctAnswerText: Escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
questions.explanation: Look for escape routes at intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones. These are places where hazards are common.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a green arrow before you can turn in that direction.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, each motorcycle should pass one at a time. One rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Clothing with reflective material.
A short-sleeved shirt.
Dark-colored clothing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothing with reflective material.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear clothing with reflective material to make yourself more visible. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.
